explanations: There is no defect. Status has symmetric MarshalJSON and UnmarshalJSON, so only known names are accepted and emitted, and a zero Status fails loudly instead of leaking a number. Ticket.MarshalJSON uses a method-less alias type to avoid infinite recursion and turns a nil Tags slice into [] so clients never see null for a list. Requests are decoded with a size limit, DisallowUnknownFields, and a check for trailing data. Responses are encoded into a buffer before WriteHeader so an encoding failure becomes a 500 instead of a truncated 200. Pointer fields in TicketPatch distinguish absent from present, which is all the patch semantics here need.

UnmarshalJSON lowercases the name before the lookup, so "SOLVED" maps to StatusSolved. Because Status is a pointer in TicketPatch, the decoder allocates it and calls the pointer-receiver method. The response is encoded through MarshalJSON, which emits the lowercase name. Choices 0 and 2 ignore the ToLower, and choice 3 is wrong because custom unmarshalers are honored for pointer fields.

decodeStrict sets DisallowUnknownFields on the decoder, so decoding into NewTicket, which has no priority field, returns an error and create replies 400 with its message. Nothing is stored. Choices 0 and 2 assume default lenient decoding, and choice 3 invents a rule the decoder does not have.

Ticket.MarshalJSON replaces a nil Tags with an empty slice, so tags is []. AssigneeID has no omitempty, so a nil pointer is written as null. DueAt has omitempty, so a nil pointer drops the key. Choice 0 would happen without the custom marshaler, and choices 2 and 3 mismatch the struct tags.
